headReviewed: the handoff push above ab06eee9dbde (code head 9dda974d2bc7)
round: narrowed round: review 5722761728's three findings and two Minors against the ownership rule, the composer lock, spentKept, and the round's tests
accepted: Review 5722761728's three findings are fixed on the ownership rule: a taken-back confirmation puts its marks back (put-back insert), a hold takes only rows its own claim owns, and a release clears only the hold. ClaimKeptDecisions clears the void hold it overrides. Each has a test that fails with only its fix reverted (deep review ran the mutations).

Every naming path reads through UnclaimedKept's lock and claims all-or-nothing in one transaction under SerializeFacts: admission, QueueCatchUp from ready, HandOverKept, Adopt, spentKept and rootTask.

Lock order: every writer goes parked_decisions then readmitted_approvals. A deadlock is possible only between two single multi-row statements, and every aborted side retries (fact replay, outbox retry, saved/settle) with at worst a second telling.
spentKept loses nothing and tells no wrong tree; the DropCatchUps telling-wide lease guard is right.

keyFindings.description: main's required ci-ok is failure because test failed at the code head: intake TestConsumePreparesAnIssueEventsRepositoryBeforeApplyingIt (prepared 3 times, want 2, after a NATS permissions violation on $JS.API.STREAM.MSG.GET) and launcher TestTheContainersStopEndsEveryRoleWithinOneStopGrace (stop took 2.73 s). Neither package's tested behaviour is changed by this branch, so both read as flakes, but a red required check is not approved.
GitHub reports #2163 CONFLICTING/DIRTY against main at 03:15Z, so no pull_request run can judge a new head. Forward-merge main, then the new head's CI decides the test failures.

The all-or-nothing check cannot catch the race its comment describes: with the lock removed, the second composer's UPDATE re-checks against its old snapshot and claims anyway (deep review's mutation). The lock is what prevents it; say so.

The put-back runs on every unconfirmed write, not only a taken-back confirmation; the comment and daemon/workflow.go:513 state the narrower condition. Make the comment state what the insert does and why it is safe.

pg_locks is read cluster-wide; filter on the second composer's backend pid. TestAHoldReleaseLeavesAClaimThatCounts' second assertion stays green with the release change reverted; spentKept's claims==0 branch has no test.
'the decisions wait in the outbox, never in the table alone' is false when the root does not hear (CatchUpTheTreesOwed writes nothing).
Still describes the old DropCatchUps rule (one live lease) rather than the telling-wide one.

notFindings: A CHECK constraint for claimed-or-held, one shared helper for supersededKept/spentKept and for the hold-ownership SQL, and moving the UnclaimedKept pairing into EnqueueNaming are maintainability, not faults.
